intro: Village Voice uses one Speaker.bot queue for alert acknowledgements and optional viewer TTS. Twitch and Kick use native rewards; YouTube and TikTok use Viewer Foundation points and a command.

sections.title: 1. Speaker.bot setup
sections.notice: Create a Voice Alias in Speaker.bot first, enter that exact alias here, connect Speaker.bot inside Streamer.bot, approve only Speak, then test before enabling live speech.

sections.title: 2. Viewer TTS requests
sections.notice: Recommended Twitch/Kick reward — title: Village Voice - TTS; cost: 500; color: #7C3AED; description: 'Enter a message for the stream to read aloud. Safety filters and cooldowns apply.' Viewer input required. Enable Skip Reward Queue on Twitch because Village Voice queues accepted speech directly. YouTube and TikTok use !speak plus Viewer Foundation points. Kick has no documented automatic refund method.

sections.title: 3. Request length and safety
sections.notice: These are creator safety caps for spoken text, not claims about each platform's entire chat limit. Links and control characters are removed before speech.

sections.title: 4. Speaking overlay
sections.notice: The hosted card shows the validated avatar when available and reveals words progressively using estimated speech timing. Speaker.bot's C# request method does not expose exact playback completion.

sections.title: 5. Alert speech
sections.notice: Thank-you text and viewer-written text are separate. Viewer alert messages remain off until explicitly selected.

sections.title: 7. Financial and spam thresholds
sections.notice: Use thresholds to keep small repeated events visual-only. Like alerts can still appear every 100 likes while Village Voice speaks only at the selected total-like interval.

sections.title: 9. Emergency controls
sections.notice: Pause, Resume, and Stop control future StreamBridge requests. Use Speaker.bot Clear Pending or Stop Speaking to immediately clear audio already queued inside Speaker.bot.
